rv.q: “American Idiot,” directed by Michael Mayer and performed with galvanizing intensity by a terrific cast, detonates a fierce aesthetic charge in this ho-hum Broadway season.
'American Idiot' is an exuberant assault - a slick and tough 95-minute package of alienated suburban youth, media overstimulation and seamless, high-concept theatricality.
"American Idiot" is a rousing, cannily assembled stage spectacle.
Green Day's punk-rock song cycle gets a vibrant staging that's heavy on style and emotion but light on narrative coherence.

Although the original concept album is reasonably cohesive, it's a thin premise on which to base a musical, and the show's book, by the band's Armstrong and director Michael Mayer, doesn't manage to flesh it out sufficiently.
Wildly diverting to look it, the show has the barest wisp of a story and minimal character development.
By the time it ends, 90 minutes later, you may feel more numbed than stirred.
Telling its story largely through music and movement with only a smattering of dialogue, “Idiot” never manages to make us care about the fate of its thinly drawn characters.
The show works best when it focuses on the emotional journey of its characters rather than trying to be a literal adaptation of Green Day's concept album.
I found them to be brain-numbingly dull.
But this musical—a half-exploitative, half-lobotomized attempt to fake a youthgasm—has none of the power of that album.
Not that you'll need much prodding to fall for this fundamentally affectionate, surprisingly uplifting show.
The point here isn’t story but style, and American Idiot delivers its predictable message (life, especially its US variety, can sometimes suck) in spectacular fashion.
Still, punk nihilism and showbiz spirit-fingers are uneasy bedfellows.

Even with Gallagher thrashing around at its center, American Idiot satisfies in spite of all that's working against it—including the passage of time (and a presidency) that's rendered much of its discontent obsolete.
Some will see 'American Idiot' as an elaborate music video for the big stage while others will find it revelatory.
Still, 90 minutes of barbaric yawp does not an opera, punk or otherwise, make.
Yet the show feels puzzlingly lackluster, like a last-minute birthday gift originally purchased for somebody else.
Still, the headache you’re getting may be one you want to keep as the show is irresistibly propelled by the suggestive power of youth.
On purely musical and visual levels, 'American Idiot' reaches some exhilarating heights.
I was hoping to experience something new in this new-generation rock opera, but American Idiot is instead a long string of cliches.
